title: Import queue log
description: What a writer did with the queue, on the writer's own branch. A writer never edits the queue: it appends here, and the planner reads both branches' logs to know what is done. An item whose id a log holds is finished, however it finished. Like the queue it is not a record, and tools/validate.mjs is the only thing that checks it. M90 §1.

entries.description: One entry per item the writer took, in the order it took them. Appended, never rewritten: a fire that refused an item is news the planner reads once and the record of it stays.

id.description: The queue item's id, which is what says the item is done.

fired.description: When the fire that took the item ran, to the minute, in UTC.

status.description: `written`: the event and every edge it could keep — since 13 October 2026 (M91) an event is imported whether or not an edge stands, so `written` with no edge is the event alone, with the refusals of the edges it queued listed. `partial`: the event and some of the edges, the rest in `refusals`. `refused`: nothing at all, because the lead could not be read (`summary-missing`) or the import wrote no record. `skipped`: the atlas, on either branch, holds the item already, by its Wikidata id or by its article's title.

written.description: What reached disk. Empty of everything on a refusal or a skip.

place.description: The place record the import created for this event, where it created one. A place it found already here is not written and is not named.

note.description: One line about the entry as a whole, where the status alone does not say enough: which record already carried the item on a skip, or why the import wrote no event at all. Not a refusal against an edge — those are below, by index and by code.

refusals.description: What the writer would not write and why, by code. The planner reads these: `quote-not-found` comes back to it to be re-read, and the others are its own judgement to revise.

edge.description: Which of the item's edges, by index into its own `edges` list. Absent or null where the refusal is not about an edge — a parent that could not be filed, or a record whose lead could not be read (`summary-missing`).

reason.description: The code, from a closed list: `quote-not-found` (the revision's text does not carry the sentence), `chronology` (A15(5): the sentence states an order and no cause), `parent-to-child` (an edge between a record and one of its own umbrellas, A14), `type` (not one of the five), `endpoint-missing` (an end that is not an active event of this atlas), `confidence` (a `consensus` edge resting on Wikipedia alone, or on one source: rules 9 and 22), `parent` (an umbrella that is not an active event, or whose span does not contain the event's start: rule 24 and A6), `arrow-of-time` (a cause that starts after its effect: rule 4), `already-held` (the edge is already a record, and a writer never rewrites one), `summary-missing` (the import could not read the lead and wrote its placeholder summary, so the record was taken back off disk: rules card 2), `parent-cycle` (a queued parent that is already part of the record: rule 24), `edge-cycle` (the reverse of an edge already active: rule 5).

detail.description: What the writer found, in one line, so the planner does not have to guess which of its own decisions was wrong.
